artworks.title: Le chapeau qu'on rapporte de Paris
artworks.creditLine: Corcoran Collection (Gift of Dr. Armand Hammer, 1983)
artworks.description: The image shows a scene with two people visible from head to toe. The man on the left is standing, leaning slightly forward with one hand in a pocket or holding onto something, looking at the woman opposite him. He has a serious facial expression with a long nose and wears a long dark coat over lighter pants. His hair appears to be thinning and swept back. The woman is standing with her body turned slightly to the side, facing towards the man and the viewer. Her facial features are not clearly visible, but she appears to have a serious demeanor. Her hair is gathered up with a white feather decoration. She is dressed in a voluminous long gown with a bodice and draped fabric, likely with a shawl over her shoulders. In the background, a series of hats are displayed, suggesting a shop setting. The backdrop appears to be a softly shaded scene with vertical lines indicating wooden panels or shelves behind the characters.

artworks.title: J'aimerais autant voir un ouragan ...
artworks.creditLine: Corcoran Collection
artworks.description: This is a drawing of an elaborate dress on a mannequin-like stand in a garden with a man observing it. The drawing shows a voluminous, structured dress with a crinoline, situated in a garden setting. The dress is positioned centrally and appears to be mounted on a mannequin or structure, as it lacks arms and a visible body above the waistline. To the right, a man stands with his back towards the viewer, wearing a hat and long coat. The garden is detailed with lines and shading, suggesting foliage and pathways, against a backdrop of trees and shrubs.

artworks.title: Boulevard de Strasbourg, Corsets
artworks.creditLine: Corcoran Collection (Bequest of Marchal E. Landgren, 1983)
artworks.description: This black-and-white photograph shows a storefront with multiple mannequins displayed in the window. The mannequins don't have heads or arms, and they show torsos with thin waists and round hips. Various corsets with bows and ruffles are arranged neatly on the mannequins seen through the windows. On the left, the door of the storefront is partially open, and one mannequin in a corset hangs in front of the door. The sign above reads "CORSETS," with smaller signage on the window and door. The window on the left of the door appears to show folded corsets or other corsetry accessories.

artworks.title: Passager ayant payé ... pour se rendre a New-York ...
artworks.creditLine: Corcoran Collection
artworks.description: The image shows a seated man with his arms wrapped around his knees, looking towards the right where a large ship is visible on the water. The man wears a plaid cap, a coat, and checkered pants. Beside him on the ground is a large bag. In the background is a body of water with a large ship partially submerged or sinking. The scene is depicted in a sketch style.

artworks.title: Les comédiens de société
artworks.creditLine: Corcoran Collection
artworks.description: This is a drawing of a theatre scene with an audience watching actors on stage. The image shows a theatre setting with multiple figures seated as an audience facing a stage where two actors are performing. On the left side, four figures are reacting to the performance, one of them gesturing towards the stage. The stage is set with a backdrop and two characters standing close to each other, possibly in an embrace. The detailed expressions of the audience and the actors, as well as the intricate lines suggesting the crowded environment, capture the theatrical atmosphere effectively.

artworks.title: Landscapes
artworks.creditLine: Corcoran Collection (Museum exchange, through a gift of Emily Sargent and Violet Ormond, 1960)
artworks.description: The image shows a dual sketch on a single sheet. In the upper section, there is a gently rolling mountain range with sparse trees. The lower sketch features a water body, possibly a river or lake, with reflections and faint markers. Brushstrokes are fine and subtle, primarily in pencil. The color palette is monochromatic, with light pencil on beige or tan paper. In the foreground, there are sketchy indications of trees and land formations, transitioning into more indistinct lines and shapes in the distance.

artworks.title: Four Figures
artworks.medium: graphite and ink wash on fabric mounted to paperboard
artworks.creditLine: Corcoran Collection (Gift of Emily Crane Chadbourne, 1931)
artworks.description: This is a drawing of four nude figures in a relaxed, reclining position. The drawing features fluid line work outlining the contours of the figures. The background is plain, focusing attention on the arrangement of the figures. The drawing conveys a sense of calmness and intimacy among the figures, which appear to be composed with a graceful quality.

artworks.title: Une méprise a l'odéon ...
artworks.creditLine: Corcoran Collection
artworks.description: The image shows two individuals in a theater setting. The man is in formal attire with a top hat and overcoat, gesturing with his hand as if speaking. The woman beside him wears a bonnet and cape, with a surprised expression. The background includes curtains, seats, and another figure on stage.

artworks.title: Le Traite des blanches (The White Slave Trade)
artworks.medium: etching on laid Van Gelder paper
artworks.creditLine: Corcoran Collection (Gift of E. Gerald Lamboley, 1993)
artworks.description: The image shows two individuals depicted from the mid-thigh up, positioned side by side. The person on the left is a young woman standing with her head slightly bowed and eyes cast downward, having long hair that flows down past her shoulders. Her facial features are delicate with a gentle profile. She appears to be wearing a loose, off-the-shoulder dress with pleats. The person on the right is an older woman facing slightly towards the younger woman. Her head is turned in profile, and she wears a large, ornate hat adorned with a ribbon and bow. She has a full figure wrapped in a voluminous shawl, and she holds a closed, pointed umbrella in front of her. The background consists of vertical, linear strokes giving a textured appearance.

artworks.title: Pas mèche!!!
artworks.creditLine: Corcoran Collection (Gift of Dr. Armand Hammer, 1983)
artworks.description: This is a drawing of a figure lifting a heavy object labeled "Réparation Monarchique." The figure has exaggerated features and is depicted leaning forward with one arm extended back, as if struggling to lift a trapezoidal object from the ground. The object bears an inscription related to monarchy. The scene conveys a sense of struggle through the character's posture and musculature. The background is minimalistic.

artworks.title: Baptism
artworks.creditLine: Corcoran Collection (Gift of E. Gerald Lamboley, 1993)
artworks.description: Three individuals are depicted in the image, each positioned side by side. The central figure, a young woman, faces towards the left with closed eyes and a cloth wrapped around her head. She wears a dark cloak with a circular brooch at her collar. To her left is an old man in profile with a cap and dark clothing. On her right is another older man in profile with a cloak and raised collar, appearing to hold his hands together. The background consists of vertically sketched lines.

artworks.title: Light and Shadow: The Shadows of Dissipation Falling upon the Poor
artworks.medium: graphite, ink wash, and gouache on wove paper
artworks.creditLine: Corcoran Collection (Museum Purchase, Membership Association Fund, 1951)
artworks.description: The image depicts two women, one standing and the other seated. The standing woman has soft facial features and long hair, wearing a long gown. She is holding her gown in front of her with her hands. A small dog is shown beside her. The seated woman has her face in her hand, looking to her right. She wears a simple dress and a shawl around her shoulders. The background includes a streetlamp on the left and a wall with indistinct text on the right.

artworks.title: Study for "The Defeat of the Floating Batteries at Gibraltar"
artworks.medium: pen and brown ink with graphite on laid paper
artworks.creditLine: Corcoran Collection (Gift of Mrs. Josephine Boardman Crane, 1956)
artworks.description: The image shows a composition of curved lines converging to form an abstract representation. In the center, there are figures interwoven in fluid movements. The arrangement of forms resembles a wave or a group of bodies moving upwards. The figures are elongated and expressive, conveying tension and motion evocative of struggle or ascension.

artworks.title: Customs Shed
artworks.medium: pen and black ink with wash on wove paper
artworks.creditLine: Corcoran Collection (Museum Purchase, 1963)
artworks.description: This is a drawing of a customs scene at a port. The image shows trunks, bags, and goods being handled and inspected at a customs office, with a stream of individuals moving through the large space. The foreground includes people engaging with luggage, conversing, or queuing at the customs house. In the background, more figures are crowded together, suggesting a busy port atmosphere. The drawing is detailed, emphasizing travel and inspection processes with fine lines and a monochromatic palette.

artworks.title: Un joli calembour
artworks.creditLine: Corcoran Collection (Gift of Dr. Armand Hammer, 1983)
artworks.description: The image shows an interior scene with two individuals seated at a wooden table, both visible from the waist up. The person on the left sits on a stool, leaning forward with long hair and elongated facial features. They are wearing a sleeveless top and appear to be holding cards. The person on the right has short, tousled hair, wears a hat and spectacles, and is shirtless with a sheet around their waist. Both are engaged in a card game with cards, glasses, and a bottle on the table. In the dimly lit room, two figures can be seen walking away wrapped in towels or robes.

artworks.title: George Raleigh Dearborn
artworks.artist: Charles B. J. Févret de Saint-Mémin
artworks.medium: charcoal and pastel on pink prepared paper
artworks.creditLine: Corcoran Collection (Museum Purchase, 1951)
artworks.description: The image depicts a portrait of a man in profile view facing left. The man has curly hair, a prominent nose, and a slightly protruding chin. He wears a white shirt and a dark buttoned-up jacket. The portrait has a monochromatic color scheme and a smooth texture. The background is a soft peach color. No jewelry or objects are visible in the portrait.

artworks.title: John Carlyle Herbert
artworks.artist: Charles B. J. Févret de Saint-Mémin
artworks.medium: charcoal and pastel on pink prepared paper
artworks.creditLine: Corcoran Collection (Gift of Thomas A. Herbert and Robert Beverley Herbert in memory of their father, Edward Herbert, and Guy F. Herbert, W. Pinkney Herbert, and R. Beverley Herbert, Sr., 1964)
artworks.description: The image shows a head and shoulders portrait of a man in profile, with his body turned to the right. He has a prominent nose, a defined jawline, and eyes looking forward. His hair is styled in short curls and he is dressed in a dark double-breasted coat with a high collar. A white neck cravat is visible underneath. The background is a uniform reddish-brown color.

artworks.title: Le départ de l'hiver
artworks.creditLine: Corcoran Collection
artworks.description: This is a drawing of a caricature scene involving two figures in military attire interacting with a figure representing winter. The drawing depicts two officers standing in an authoritative posture facing an anthropomorphized embodiment of winter. The figure representing winter is cloaked in heavy garments with icicles protruding from it. Large, leafless branches and birds flying overhead are also depicted in the scene. Text at the bottom of the image reads "LE DEPART DE L'HIVER."

artworks.title: Building by a Dam
artworks.medium: graphite over watercolor on wove paper
artworks.creditLine: Corcoran Collection (Museum Purchase, 1948)
artworks.description: The image depicts a rocky landscape with a small waterfall flowing into a stream or pool of water. In the background, there is a wooden building on a rock and a low structure or fence extending towards the center-right. The artwork features delicate and sketch-like brushwork and pencil strokes, capturing the textures of rocks and foliage with light, varied lines. The color palette is muted with soft greys, off-whites, and a hint of light blue sky. Trees and shrubs are visible in the distance, enhancing the sense of depth without disrupting the tranquil atmosphere created by the flowing water and rustic structure.

artworks.title: Devant le tableau de M. G. Moreau
artworks.creditLine: Corcoran Collection
artworks.description: The image shows five elderly individuals mostly depicted from the waist up. They appear to be crowded and focused on something, potentially engaged in conversation. The people have distinct facial features and expressions, such as large eyes and wrinkles. They have varying hairstyles, some neatly combed and others sparse. The individuals are dressed in period attire with long coats and high collars. One person wears a top hat and glasses and holds an open book or paper. The setting seems to be an interior space with elaborate wood paneling and smaller windows, hinting at an exhibition or gallery.

artworks.title: Distribution de vivres un jour d'extra
artworks.creditLine: Corcoran Collection (Gift of Dr. Armand Hammer, 1983)
artworks.description: This is a drawing depicting a group of caricatured figures engaging in a provision distribution scene. Two figures in the foreground are holding and receiving knife-like objects on a tray. In the background, more figures are gathered around a container labeled "Lampions égalité." The figures have exaggerated features and are portrayed in a satirical manner. The scene conveys a sense of chaos and humor typical of political or social cartoons from that era.

artworks.title: Les russes encourageant l'agriculture
artworks.creditLine: Corcoran Collection (Gift of Dr. Armand Hammer, 1983)
artworks.description: This is a drawing of three humanoid figures engaged in an agricultural activity. The drawing depicts a scene where two figures appear to be bent over pulling a plow, with exaggerated facial features and small, skinny frames. Each figure is awkwardly hunched over. The third figure, riding a horse, is positioned between them, wielding a stick or agricultural tool. This figure also has an exaggerated expression, with thick eyebrows and a tattered hat. The figures are set against a minimalistic landscape with horizontal lines suggesting a field.

artworks.title: Bigre! ... j'ai eu tort de me mettre ...
artworks.creditLine: Corcoran Collection (Gift of Dr. Armand Hammer, 1983)
artworks.description: This is a drawing of a figure holding up a large globe labeled "Europe" and "Asie". The globe is detailed with outlines of continents, specifically Europe and part of Asia, and includes some terrestrial markings. The character appears to be taken aback or surprised, with dramatic motion lines indicating effort or instability. The features and attire of the character are exaggerated for comedic effect, typical of political or satirical cartoons. There is a caption at the bottom. The style of the drawing is reminiscent of political cartoons by artists such as Honoré Daumier.

artworks.title: Un amateur difficile
artworks.creditLine: Corcoran Collection
artworks.description: This is a drawing of an art exhibition scene. The black and white drawing shows a crowded space with frames of paintings on the walls. In the foreground, an individual is seated and cutting food on a plate with a fork and knife. In the background, more individuals are gathered around, likely discussing or observing the art on display. The style of the drawing is reminiscent of caricature, with exaggerated features of the attendees. It portrays a salon or exhibition setting, capturing social dynamics and interactions among the guests.
